subject.title: Feature: force media delivery as document attachment (e.g. #doc)

question: Should OpenClaw support force-document behavior beyond the current per-call `forceDocument`/`asDocument` knobs, and if so should the public contract be `MEDIA:#doc`, a channel-level default, or a narrower channel/plugin-specific setting?
rationale: Current code already solves explicit per-call sends; the remaining request creates either new model-facing syntax or new channel config/default behavior, both of which repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive product/API surface.

options.title: Keep Per-Call Canonical
options.body: Keep `--force-document` and `asDocument` as the supported contract for now and require a sponsored narrower proposal before adding syntax or config defaults.

options.title: Define `MEDIA:#doc` Syntax
options.body: Specify fragment parsing and media-kind semantics in the shared media pipeline, then thread it through affected delivery paths with tests and live proof.

options.title: Add Default-Off Channel Setting
options.body: Design a per-channel or per-account default that preserves current behavior by default, documents override behavior, and proves upgrades do not change existing sends.

recommendation.title: Keep Per-Call Canonical
recommendation.body: Keep `--force-document` and `asDocument` as the supported contract for now and require a sponsored narrower proposal before adding syntax or config defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a source-contract/config direction decision, and recent history points to Peter Steinberger on the current contract wording and delivery surfaces.
